Hi Chloe,

Thanks again for the demo last week. Our engineering team is finalizing the Dedicated commitment and needs concrete sizing guidance. Two constraints to consider:

- Production inference will use our custom retrieval-augmented prompts with an active context window that averages ~45k tokens and occasionally spikes to ~120k tokens for deep case lookups.
- We plan to run a few model variants: a tuned 13B for high-throughput async ops and a 70B variant for high-fidelity, low-qps interactions.

Specifically we need:
1) Expected GPU memory footprint (per-GPU) for both variants for typical and peak context lengths; include KV cache sizing and prefix retention assumptions.
2) How different precision profiles (FP16 vs INT8/GPTQ-style) affect both memory and expected throughput/latency.
3) Recommended reserved pool mix and headroom to cover spikes while keeping cost predictable.

Can you send something we can share with procurement by EOD Friday? We also expect a short runbook describing fallbacks (smaller model / reduced retained context) for SLA events.

— Alicia

Subject: FW: Dedicated sizing for long-context models — sizing estimate (draft)

Team — draft sizing calculations for Veridian. I kept the assumptions explicit so procurement can see the tradeoffs. Pasting the key sections below; full workbook attached to the outbound mail to Alicia.

=== Summary assumptions ===
- Model variants: tuned-13B (optimize throughput), tuned-70B (high-fidelity).
- Typical qps: 13B = 40 qps (steady), 70B = 2 qps (steady); spikes up to 60 qps and 6 qps respectively (rare, 95th percentile).
- Primary context retention approach: keep most-recent 32k tokens hot in KV per request; prefix segments older than 32k are stored in fast blob store and rehydrated on-demand for <5% of requests. Veridian asked for 120k spike retention case — we provide a fallback plan for that.

=== Memory & GPU footprint (per model variant) ===
Assumptions: 1 token KV entry ~ bytes_per_token where bytes_per_token depends on model hidden size and head layout; here we use empirically measured numbers from bench runs on A100-80GB-equivalent:
- tuned-13B (huge embeddings / 2048 dim KV)
  - KV per token ~ 110 bytes (both key+value + metadata)
  - Model params in FP16 ~ 13B * 2 bytes = ~26 GB; plus optimizer/overhead ~ 3 GB => base model ~29 GB
  - FP16 runtime + activation headroom ~ +4 GB => FP16 total approx 33 GB
  - INT8/GPTQ-style quantization (post-calibration) reduces param storage to ~8 GB on GPU (with ~2 GB for dequant kernels) => ~10 GB base; activation/kv memory still applies
  - KV impact: 32k tokens * 110 bytes = ~3.5 MB (note: per-batch/beam multipliers apply) — this is small relative to params for 13B; for 120k tokens ~13.2 MB.
  - Conclusion: 13B FP16 comfortably fits on an 80 GB class GPU with room for batching; quantized 13B allows denser packing and ~2-3x more concurrent streams per GPU.

- tuned-70B (large attention KV footprint)
  - KV per token ~ 250 bytes (wider layers and multihead state)
  - Model params FP16 ~ 70B * 2 bytes = ~140 GB; runtime sharding / tensor-slicing required across multiple GPUs. We assume model parallel 4-way on 80GB-class GPUs => per-GPU param memory ~35 GB + overhead ~6 GB => ~41 GB base/replica
  - FP16 total per GPU (including activations for a 32k hot window) ~ +16 GB => ~57 GB per GPU (fits on 80GB but with limited headroom).
  - INT8/GPTQ-style quant reduces model param footprint per GPU to ~13-16 GB, freeing 20-25 GB for larger KV or batching. However dequant and fused-kernel costs add ~3-4 GB runtime overhead.
  - KV impact: 32k tokens * 250 bytes = ~8 MB per request hot; 120k tokens ~30 MB. For multi-request batching concurrency these add up but remain primarily in host or managed cache unless pinned on-device.

=== Throughput & GPU counts (recommended pool mixes) ===
Two commitment scenarios: Conservative (SLA-first) and Optimized (cost-first with dynamic offload):
1) Conservative (target p99 latency 300–500ms for native requests on 13B; 1.2–1.8s p99 on 70B)
  - 13B: use 80GB GPU nodes, 1 model-replica per GPU, target 40 steady qps => ~6 GPUs for steady; +30% headroom => 8 GPUs.
  - 70B: 4-way MP across 4x80GB GPUs per model replica; steady 2 qps per replica -> need 3 replicas for steady (6 qps capacity); add 1 replica for headroom => total 4 replicas => 16 GPUs.
  - Total GPUs conservative: 24 GPUs (mix: 8 for 13B, 16 for 70B).

2) Optimized (aggressive quant + prefix offload, target slightly higher tail latencies for very large history)
  - 13B INT8 pack: expect ~2.5x density => 8 GPUs -> 3 GPUs equivalent (consolidated) for steady; recommend 4 GPUs with burst headroom.
  - 70B GPTQ: reduce per-replica GPUs from 4->2 effective by memory packing + kernel fusion for scaled batches; recommend 6 GPUs total to maintain ~6 qps steady with on-demand rehydration for spikes.
  - Total GPUs optimized: ~10 GPUs (mix: 4 for 13B quantized, 6 for 70B quantized).

=== Spike handling & runbook highlights ===
- For full 120k retention: prefer prefix offload + rehydrate path. Reserve a small pool of 'rehydration workers' (2–4 GPUs) that can fetch prefix segments and stitch them into the hot KV on-demand; do not keep 120k pinned in KV for all requests — cost-prohibitive.
- Canary & fallback: route to tuned-13B when 70B queue depth exceeds threshold or when rehydration latency crosses 400ms. Provide a degraded-response mode that truncates prefix to most-recent 32k and appends link to full record.
- Monitoring: token-level cost, KV hit-rate, rehydration latency, and per-GPU memory-pressure alarms (critical at >85% usage).

Notes on numbers: these are bench-derived estimates; real run results depend on batching patterns, request shapes, and the quantization toolchain used. For the deck to procurement we should show both scenarios with rough monthly cost delta.

Hi Alicia — attaching the concise runbook (memory_runbook_v1.pdf) and the capacity workbook. Key recommendations up front:

- Procurement-friendly commitment tiers: 10 GPU reserved (optimized) and 25 GPU reserved (conservative). We mapped monthly support hours and SLA uplift per tier in the workbook.
- Recommended operational guardrails: keep hot KV pinned to 32k tokens by default; allow on-demand rehydration to 120k for <5% traffic.
- Precision pathing: enable INT8/GPTQ for 13B in production day-1; stage GPTQ for 70B (validation + quality checks) and enable for burst windows after 2-week observation.

Next steps: Alicia — if procurement wants numbers we will finalize the monthly committed units and include line items for rehydration-worker hours and optional premium support. Happy to hop on a call Monday to review with your finance team.

Thanks,
